rationale: Zernio was introduced primarily to reach TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook -- platforms the prior YouTube-only direct adapter never covered. The main long-form episode is a documentary-style YouTube asset; it is not edited for the short-form-native platforms and has no approved editorial plan for Facebook long-form distribution. Shorts are already produced as 9:16 short-form content and are the natural fit for all four platforms. Facebook is deliberately excluded for the main episode pending a separate editorial/distribution decision -- this is NOT because Facebook lacks technical video support.
tiktok_privacy_value_source: docs.zernio.com/platforms/tiktok, live-fetched 2026-08-22 -- the documented tiktokSettings.privacy_level enum is exactly {PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE, MUTUAL_FOLLOW_FRIENDS, FOLLOWER_OF_CREATOR, SELF_ONLY}. PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE is the value matching Hypogeum's intended public-distribution policy -- never invented, this exact string is the documented enum member.
known_gaps: Facebook main_episode=false is a deliberate scope decision for this policy version, not a technical limitation -- see rationale.

This policy only declares WHICH platform/deliverable-class combinations are permitted. It does not itself declare per-platform schedule times (see scheduling_policy_v1.json's bundle_cycle_policy, which remains deliverable_id-keyed and applies to every platform that deliverable is routed to) or canonical captions (see shorts_captions -- not yet approved, see the cross-platform readiness checkpoint).

v1.1.0 adds tiktok.shorts.privacy=PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE (was missing in v1.0.0, confirmed as a real blocker in the cross-platform readiness checkpoint). Instagram/Facebook have no documented privacy field to configure.
installation: NOT applied to any database. To install (idempotent, preserves every other existing field -- see hypogeum.channel_config.update_channel_operations_profile()): update_channel_operations_profile(channel_id='hypogeum', platform_deliverable_policy=<this file's 'platform_deliverable_policy' object>). Requires explicit operator approval -- not performed by this artifact's presence alone.
